p: Replay and inspect Behavior Tree execution after the fact.

The default Behavior Tree debugger only tells you what an agent is doing right now. Behavior Tree Graph Viewer works from Visual Logger data instead: record a session (or open a .bvlog someone else captured), then scrub a timeline and watch the real Behavior Tree graph light up frame by frame, with that agent's Blackboard next to it.
BT Graph Viewer replaying a captured session
Useful when the bug happened three minutes ago, on a machine that isn't yours.

BT Graph Viewer registers a native Unreal Toolset, so any AI client wired into Unreal's Toolset Registry (the engine's MCP server) can drive the viewer directly. Your AI client lists it as BTGraphViewerToolset among the available toolsets.
Every call drives the same viewer window a human uses. There is no parallel code path, and all of it stays read-only with respect to your assets.
The toolset lives in the plugin's BTGraphViewerAI module and is available as soon as BT Graph Viewer is enabled. If you never use AI tooling, nothing calls it and you can ignore this page.

Status
Toolset Registry is Experimental
Toolset Registry ships with the engine but is disabled by default. BT Graph Viewer declares it as a dependency, so Unreal enables it for you.
Enable BT Graph Viewer as usual (see Getting Started) and restart the editor. In Edit → Plugins you will find Toolset Registry enabled next to it, turned on for you.
From your AI client, BTGraphViewerToolset then shows up in list_toolsets.
Typical loop: LoadCapture → SelectAgent → SetFrame → GetViewerState. That is enough for an assistant to walk a capture and explain why an agent did what it did.

Full state: active nodes, Blackboard, and the node ↔ execution-index map.
The viewer displays your real Behavior Tree asset, not a copy. It is therefore built so it can never modify it:
the graph editor is created read-only, and node and pin widgets refuse drag, drop, double-click and connection edits;
decorator/service drag-drop is cancelled before any drop is delivered;
Delete, Backspace, Ctrl+X and Alt+click are swallowed while the cursor is over the graph;
any modification that still slips through is reverted;
the asset's bEditable flag and its nodes' read-only flags are never touched, so opening the same tree in the normal Behavior Tree editor afterwards behaves exactly as before.
Your Behavior Tree assets are never dirtied and never need saving because you looked at them. An automation test (BTGraphViewer.ReadOnly.NoAssetMutation) enforces this.
Run from the editor console:
or via Tools → Test Automation, category BTGraphViewer.
Editor only. By design, this is a debugging tool.

The Behavior Tree asset referenced by a capture must exist in the currently open project. The viewer resolves it by asset name through the Asset Registry. If it isn't found, the Graph panel says so instead of showing anything.
Gameplay Debugger sync covers PIE/Game worlds and a single local player.
Pressing Stop stops Visual Logger recording globally, exactly as the default Visual Logger window's Stop button does.

If the Behavior Tree has been structurally edited (nodes added, removed, or reordered) since the capture was recorded, the viewer cannot detect it. Node highlighting is matched by execution index, which Unreal recomputes from the tree's current shape, so an old capture can end up highlighting the wrong node with no warning. Keep captures close to the version of the tree they were recorded against, especially before sharing one.
Behavior Tree not found

l: The Graph panel says the Behavior Tree wasn't found.
p: The capture's Behavior Tree asset must exist in the open project. Open the project the capture came from, or make sure the asset is present.

l: Can I open a capture from another machine?
p: Yes. .bvlog files come from Unreal's standard Visual Logger.

l: Does it change my Behavior Tree assets?
p: No. See Read-only guarantee.

l: Does it ship in my packaged game?
p: No. The plugin is editor-only.
